_comment: Every tool that declares reach anyone, with the reason it is safe: the in-code guard it relies on (callers list, presence proof, own-scope check, held at the Gate), or read-only. A tool with a mutating verb in its name needs a reason that names a guard; read-only does not count. PENDING reasons are tracked and shrink. test/reach-anyone.test.js fails on an anyone with no entry.

appearance.check.reason: read-only: checks a theme override, changes nothing

appearance.resolve.reason: read-only, scoped to the caller's own device and project

apps.act.reason: guard: an action that sends is refused unless it is gated, and a gated send is held at the Gate, where the person's approval (gate.approve) is the proof; what an agent may do unprompted is a timer, an alarm, a note, a reminder or the weather

apps.list.reason: read-only: lists apps and their tiers

apps.route.reason: read-only: turns words into one app action and runs nothing

apps.send.reason: guard: a presence proof is needed from every caller but a module, shown the preview, so an agent holds at the proof and cannot send silently

apps.setup.reason: guard: the callers list in code (cli, capsule, deck): it signs files and opens import windows, which no model or module may do

apps.targets.reason: read-only: an app's people and channels, cached 60 s

artifacts.archive.reason: own-scope check: scopeOf(meta) limits an agent to its own project or what it made, never the person's own artifacts; the person and modules reach all (core/artifacts scopeOf). Least sure: the artifacts owner confirms each tool calls it

artifacts.create.reason: own-scope check: scopeOf(meta) limits an agent to its own project or what it made, never the person's own artifacts; the person and modules reach all (core/artifacts scopeOf). Least sure: the artifacts owner confirms each tool calls it

artifacts.delete.reason: own-scope check: scopeOf(meta) limits an agent to its own project or what it made, never the person's own artifacts; the person and modules reach all (core/artifacts scopeOf). Least sure: the artifacts owner confirms each tool calls it

artifacts.diff.reason: read-only, scoped by the module itself

artifacts.export.reason: own-scope check: scopeOf(meta) limits an agent to its own project or what it made, never the person's own artifacts; the person and modules reach all (core/artifacts scopeOf). Least sure: the artifacts owner confirms each tool calls it

artifacts.get.reason: read-only, scoped by the module itself

artifacts.list.reason: read-only, scoped by the module itself

artifacts.move.reason: own-scope check: scopeOf(meta) limits an agent to its own project or what it made, never the person's own artifacts; the person and modules reach all (core/artifacts scopeOf). Least sure: the artifacts owner confirms each tool calls it

artifacts.public.status.reason: read-only, scoped by the module itself

artifacts.restore.reason: own-scope check via reach()/target(): restoring writes a new version of an artifact the caller may reach, never an overwrite

artifacts.search.reason: read-only, scoped by the module itself

artifacts.share.reason: outward post: held at the Gate; an agent call that the person did not ask for is refused fail-closed (the PL-M2 stopgap, core/artifacts); own-scope check via reach()/target()

artifacts.undelete.reason: own-scope check via reach()/target(): the caller must reach the artifact it brings back

artifacts.unshare.reason: own-scope check via reach()/target(): takes a public link down, the safe direction

artifacts.update.reason: own-scope check: scopeOf(meta) limits an agent to its own project or what it made, never the person's own artifacts; the person and modules reach all (core/artifacts scopeOf). Least sure: the artifacts owner confirms each tool calls it

artifacts.versions.reason: read-only, scoped by the module itself

capsule.status.reason: read-only: whether the Capsule can run here

commands.list.reason: read-only: the verbs the caller can run

link.pair.request.reason: tailnetLogin(caller) check in the tool: only the owner's own device over the tailnet may start a pairing, the code shows on that device only, and pending requests are capped

settings.changes.reason: read-only: recent changes, secret values never included

settings.get.reason: read-only: a secret's value reaches only the person, agents see names

settings.request.reason: guard: the ask check: it works only when gate.said.match finds the person's own words asking for this change in this conversation (lib/said/setting.js); no match is refused

settings.reset.reason: guard: the callers list in code (cli, local, deck, capsule), the person's own surfaces; an agent uses settings.request

settings.schema.reason: read-only: every key with its group

settings.set.reason: guard: the callers list in code (cli, local, deck, capsule), the person's own surfaces; an agent uses settings.request

settings.snapshot.reason: read-only: the settings in effect, secrets masked

settings.undo.reason: guard: the callers list in code (cli, local, deck, capsule), the person's own surfaces

sync.consent.reason: callers limited in code to capsule, cli, deck, local

sync.delete.reason: callers list in code (cli, local, deck, capsule) and a preview unless confirm: true. Weak on its own: confirm is caller-supplied and cli or local is only as strong as the socket label, so a detached child could claim cli. The socket-trust inversion (a person label only from the owner's login session) closes that; its tests include a detached child claiming cli with confirm:true, which must be refused

undo.run.reason: own-action check in the tool: the person, or whoever did the action (sameActor); the inverse runs as module:undo, never as the person, and only a declared inverse that is not outward or person-only is replayed
